title: EDUCATION: Change With It
author: Becky Abrams Wilmoth
summary: Becky Abrams Wilmoth profiles Josh Walker, the new Head of Schools at New Hope Christian School in Grants Pass, Oregon, who is launching a hybrid high school program for homeschoolers, modeled on Horizon Christian School's six-year hybrid program serving grades 2-12. Walker plans a Wednesday-Thursday on-campus schedule where hybrid students receive guided support for their online coursework, complete electives alongside full-time students, and participate in chapel, houses, sports, and quarterly Kingdom Living Days. Critically, hybrid students use 95% of the same curriculum and meet identical graduation requirements as full-time students, which allowed Cognia accreditation approval without additional steps. Online course costs are bundled into monthly tuition to remove financial barriers. Walker's dual motivation is reducing isolation for high school homeschoolers and offering parents overwhelmed by advanced academics a structured school partnership. The model demonstrates how small Christian schools can expand their service to diverse family educational needs without compromising academic integrity.
points: Same curriculum (95%) and graduation requirements as full-time students preserves accreditation integrity -- Cognia approved without additional compliance steps.
Wednesday-Thursday structure: arriving, turning in prior work, navigating online challenges, and advancing upcoming assignments.
Hybrid students fully integrated into houses, chapel, sports, and electives -- addressing the social isolation common in high school homeschooling.
Online course costs bundled into monthly tuition removes a significant financial barrier to hybrid enrollment.
Horizon Christian School's 6-year model provided a proven, replicable template for smaller schools beginning hybrid programs.
quotes: Education is changing with or without us. We have to change with it. -- Josh Walker
I believe homeschooling is a viable educational option. -- Josh Walker
Cognia gave the go-ahead because they are not really changing what they put their stamp on...the requirements are the same...graduation requirements are the same. -- Josh Walker

The keys to this being so straightforward was the fact that their hybrid program will use the same curriculum (95%) and hybrid students are enrolled and tracked the same as their full-time students. The delivery is just different.
New Hope added the cost for any online classes into the monthly tuition so that they can easily use these programs without an additional fee.
